payload.block_text: In 1997, the US enacted the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA). Under this law, it is illegal for all US persons and certain foreign securities issuers to make payments to foreign government officials to assist them in obtaining or retaining business. Since 1998, it has also applied to foreign firms and persons who, directly or indirectly, cause acts of corruption within the US. In effect since July 2024, the Foreign Extortion Prevention Technical Corrections Act complements the FCPA by criminalizing the acceptance of bribes by foreign officials and their agents. Unlike the UK and French legislation, the FCPA’s bribery provisions generally exempt facilitation payments if they are made solely to expedite a routine official action that would occur even without the payment.
